chunks: And the saying of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him):
O Allah, You do not leave the earth without a Divine Proof (Hujjah), either apparent and famed or hidden and unknown,

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Title of Imam Ali)
key_terms.خَائِفًا مَغْمُورًا: Hidden and obscure (concealed from public view)

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'Hujjah' mean in Shia theology regarding the Imamate?
ai.summary: This supplication by Imam Ali (a.s.) establishes the doctrine of *Istidraj* and the necessity of the *Hujjah* (Divine Proof) as a perpetual condition for the validity of God's blessings upon the earth. In Shia eschatology, this verse is pivotal for validating the Minor and Major Ghebah of Imam al-Hasan al-Askari (a.s.), affirming that divine guidance continues even during periods of occultation when the Imam is 'hidden and obscure' (*kha'if maghbur*).

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 183 - A saying of Amirul Momineen (a.s), “
O Allah, do not leave the earth without a Divine Proof (Hujjah), either apparent and famed or hidden and unknown,”
